title: Workload Heuristic Composer for Adaptive Request Merging and Safe Rollouts
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Goal: Build a production-ready Workload Heuristic Composer (WHC) that generates safe, per-workload recommendations for request merging and continuous batching parameters, and applies them with a guarded rollout and automated rollback.

Scope: profiling pipeline, heuristic engine, candidate suggestion API, config apply operator (canary + ramp), observability dashboard, and automated rollback circuit. This ticket covers the core composer algorithm, safety envelope definitions, and the apply/rollback automation glue. Integration tasks (SDK flags, customer-facing reporting) will be follow-ups.

Outcomes / Acceptance criteria:
- WHC produces deterministic candidate sets for at least 90% of sampled workloads in the staging cluster and surface a confidence score.
- Recommended continuous batching parameters (merge_window_ms, max_merge_size, token_grouping_hint, interarrival_dampener) reduce per-token cost by >=8% on average for profiles flagged as 'mergeable' without increasing 99th-percentile tail latency by >10% in canary tests.
- Apply operator supports shadow trial, canary at configurable traffic percentages (1%, 5%, 20%), automated health checks (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token-per-request cost), and automatic rollback if thresholds are breached.
- Rollback produces an audit artifact and opens a rollback PR with diagnostic telemetry attached.

Design notes / heuristics (high level):
1) Profiling: daily micro-profiling job aggregates sequence length distribution, inter-request interarrival histograms, model KV hit rates, and prefix reuse signatures at the 'workload' key (route + model + customer_tier). We store compact fingerprints (bloom + sketch) to detect drift.
2) Heuristic Composer: takes profile and applies layered rules in order:
   - Merge candidate filter: workloads with >30% short-seq requests (seq_len < 64) and steady interarrival (median IA < 30ms) are eligible.
   - Token-aware grouping: suggest token_grouping_hint that groups requests to target average merged sequence length ~ median_seq_len * 0.9 to avoid worst-case overrun.
   - Interarrival dampener: when interarrival variance high (CV > 1.2), recommend conservative merge_window_ms and max_merge_size to avoid latency spikes.
   - Safety envelope: compute worst-case theoretical latency delta and expected cost delta; only accept candidates where expected cost savings > safety_margin (default 5% relative) and worst-case p99 delta < safety_p99_threshold (default 12%).
3) Confidence scoring: ensemble score from sample size, drift stability (last 3 days), prefix reuse fraction, and historical successful applies for similar fingerprints. Score bucketed as low/medium/high.
4) Continuous tuning: allow WHC to emit a small monotonic adjustment proposal every promo window (e.g., reduce merge_window_ms by 5% per week) if canary tests are green and cost trend continues.

Safe apply & rollback plan:
- Phase 0 (shadow): apply config to 0% traffic, run against collected live traces in shadow mode for 12-24 hours. Metrics: simulated cost, simulated latency, mismatch rate.
- Phase 1 (canary): 1% traffic for 2 hours. Automated checks: error_rate < baseline + 0.1%, p99_latency < baseline * 1.12, token_cost_reduction >= min_savings.
- Phase 2 (ramp): 5% for 4 hours, then 20% for 8 hours. If both windows pass, mark candidate stable and proceed to gradual rollout up to 100% with health gating at each step.
- Rollback triggers: any automated check fail or manually triggered rollback. Rollback must be revertible via operator, attach diagnostics (traces, K6 or replay logs, affected request ids). Rollback PR auto-created with root cause hints from the telemetry collector.

Observability & telemetry requirements:
- New dashboards: WHC Recommendations (by workload), Canary Health, Cost Delta Over Time, Rollback Events.
- Tracing hooks: tag spans with whc_candidate_id and apply_phase.
- Telemetry retention: keep per-candidate aggregated metrics for 30 days.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for heuristic rules and confidence scoring.
- Staging e2e with canned replay traces and randomized interarrival noise.
- Load tests: synthetic spiky workload to validate rollback sensitivity and rate-limiter interactions.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- We deliberately prefer conservative initial defaults to minimize customer impact; this means lower short-term savings but faster trust-building.
- Composer will be rule-first (transparent heuristics) with a future ML-guided rescoring stage once we have labeled outcomes.
- To avoid cross-tenant interference, composer outputs config scoped to workload keys and includes tenant isolation checks for Dedicated clusters.

Follow-ups (separate tickets): SDK flags for customers, customer opt-out flow, ML rescorer exploration, UI for manual override.
